labels.text: Sign in to get started, open to everyone

S3.01.needs: an AGI account and a web browser
S3.01.note: The approval page opened in the browser is on the web app and was not reviewed.
steps: Open a terminal and type agi login, then press Enter.
Read the lines "Connecting to AGI..." and "Open this link in your browser:" and note the one-time code shown.
Open the link in a browser, check the page shows the same code, and approve it.
Back in the terminal, wait for "Waiting for authorization..." to finish.
Compare with Expected: the terminal should finish without an error and the session should be signed in.
S3.01.where: Run "agi login" in a terminal, or on first run: "Choose how to connect" > "AGI cloud"

S3.02.needs: a web browser and an email address
S3.02.note: The CLI has no sign-up screen; it only opens a browser link during agi login (apps/cli/src/oauth.rs). apps/web/features/auth/AuthEmailStep.tsx has a heading "Log in or sign up", but the browser approval page was not confirmed to reach it. Searched apps/cli/src/onboarding.rs and apps/cli/src/oauth.rs for sign-up wording.

labels.text: Memory is off for your account. Turn it on with `agi memory on`.

S3.25.note: Setup only describes memory and does not ask whether it is on; the on/off choice is the agi memory command after setup.
steps: Start agi for the first time on a machine where setup has not run, and read the "Memory" paragraph shown after the permission mode choice.
In a terminal, type agi memory status and read the answer.
Type agi memory off, then agi memory status, and check it says memory is off.
Type agi memory on, then agi memory status, and check it is back on.
Compare with Expected: the user is told about memory and can change the choice later.
S3.25.where: First-run setup shows a "Memory" paragraph; change later with "agi memory on" or "agi memory off" (check with "agi memory status")

S3.29.needs: a first run where setup has not finished, and a folder not yet trusted
S3.29.note: No command or screen-control permission step was found in setup (searched onboarding.rs for screen, folder and permission wording). Only folder trust and permission mode are set there.
steps: Start agi for the first time on a folder you have not trusted, where setup has not finished.
At "Trust This Directory", read the warning and choose "Yes, trust this directory" (or the restricted option).
Read the "Before you start:" notes about approval for file edits and shell commands.
At "Default permission mode", pick one of the three modes and read its line.
Compare with Expected: the setup covers folder trust and approval mode only; check whether it walks through commands or screen control.
S3.29.where: First-run setup: "Trust This Directory" > "Yes, trust this directory", then "Default permission mode"

labels.text: Ring the terminal bell when a long turn finishes?
Turn it off with /config set bell false.

S3.32.needs: a way to run a turn, such as a local model or a signed-in account, to hear the bell
steps: Start agi for the first time on a machine where setup has not run, and go to the question "Ring the terminal bell when a long turn finishes?".
Answer no (the default) or yes, then continue to "Press Enter to start...".
Start the app and type /config set bell true to turn the bell on later, or /config set bell false to turn it off.
Run a long task and check whether the terminal bell rings only when the setting is on.
Compare with Expected: the choice is optional, can be declined, and can be changed later.
S3.32.where: First-run setup, last question "Ring the terminal bell when a long turn finishes?"; change later with "/config set bell true" or "/config set bell false"

S3.35.note: No introduction to a first conversation was found. The closest screen is the start view in apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs, which shows "Welcome to AGI" and "Choose Local, Your key, or Managed with /model." but not what to try. Searched apps/cli/src/onboarding.rs and apps/cli/src/tui for first conversation, what to try and try wording.

S3.37.needs: Ollama or LM Studio running with a local model, and no AGI account
S3.37.note: No code was found that carries guest work into an account (searched apps/cli/src for guest, anonymous and no account wording); only the local path works without an account.
steps: Start agi for the first time on a machine that is not signed in and where setup has not run.
At "Choose how to connect", pick "Local model" (Run AI locally, no account required).
Follow the local model choice, with Ollama or LM Studio running, until the terminal says "Local model, no account needed."
Send a message in the first chat and check it answers without signing in.
Compare with Expected: the product works without an account, but no step was found that signs up later and carries guest work over.
S3.37.where: First run: "Choose how to connect" > "Local model" (no account)
